reason.description: A reason fired by the selected stored revision.

impact.description: The selected reason's served impact band. Requires reason.

lane.description: An incomplete lane in the selected stored revision.

score_min.description: Inclusive lower score bound. Pending answers without a score do not match.

score_max.description: Inclusive upper score bound, at least score_min when both are supplied.

list_match.description: The list action captured at the first answer. Requires revision first. Older answers without captured list state do not match, including none.

changed.description: true returns only assessments whose latest stored revision's decision differs from their first answer's decision (see decision); false only the others. An assessment whose first answer or latest revision has no decision yet is not changed. Cannot be combined with revision first.

AssessmentUpdatedData.description: The assessment, or the minimal notice that it expired.

id.description: The event id, equal to the NR-Webhook-Id header and across redeliveries and every endpoint the event fans out to.

created_at.description: When the event was created. Equal across redeliveries; the signing timestamp header is per delivery.

test.description: Present, and true, only on an event sent by POST /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/test: its data is a fixed example assessment, not one of the workspace's, so a receiver acknowledges it and applies nothing. Real events have no test member.

AssuranceLevel.description: Provider or OIDC assurance level, when the customer has mapped one.

AttributeAgreement.description: How far independent sources agree on one attribute: values is the number of distinct values reported, support the tables and profiles reporting any, and agreement match (one value), partial (the most reported value holds more than half the support) or mismatch. The values themselves are not served.

AuditEvent.description: One privileged workspace action with its actor, target, outcome and time. Successful data changes commit their audit evidence atomically. Sensitive exports record access before returning bytes. Details exclude secrets and subject identifiers.

id.description: Opaque, server-assigned event id: aud_ and a 26-character ULID.

workspace_id.description: The workspace id, which is also its live environment's workspace id; the test environment's is the same id with :test appended. A workspace created through the API is tnt_ and a 26-character ULID.

environment.description: The affected live or test environment. Workspace-wide changes keep live here for compatibility; affected_environment identifies their workspace scope explicitly.

action.description: What happened, as resource.verb: workspace.created, member.role_changed, member.removed, invite.created, invite.revoked, invite.accepted, key.rotated, webhook_endpoint.created, webhook_endpoint.deleted, webhook_endpoint.secret_rotated, integration.created, integration.deleted, integration.secret_rotated, list_entry.created, list_entry.deleted, webhook_endpoint.test_sent, webhook_endpoint.verification_requested, webhook_endpoint.delivery_replayed, assessment.created, assessment.outcome_recorded, assessment.deleted, account.outcome_recorded, account.enforcement_recorded, account.deleted, account.exported. A change with no finer name carries the permission it used, such as keys.live.write. New actions may appear; treat an unknown one as a change to its target.

outcome.description: succeeded: the change took effect. denied: an active member's role did not allow it, and nothing changed.

detail.description: At most 8 short facts about the change, keyed by lowercase names: the role a member was given or accepted (role), the invite an accepted member used (invite_id), the key that replaced a rotated one (new_key_id), the assessment a member's change acted on (assessment_id). Absent when there are none.

affected_environment.description: The affected scope, independent of the tenant partition storing the event. Workspace-wide membership and invitation changes use workspace.

request_id.description: Validated request correlation id, also returned in X-Request-ID, linking this event to request diagnostics. Absent on historical events without correlation.

id.description: The event id, equal to the NR-Webhook-Id header and across redeliveries and every endpoint the event fans out to.

created_at.description: When the event was created. Equal across redeliveries; the signing timestamp header is per delivery.

test.description: Present, and true, only on an event sent by POST /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/test: its data is a fixed example assessment, not one of the workspace's, so a receiver acknowledges it and applies nothing. Real events have no test member.

AuditEventList.description: GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/audit_events: one page of the workspace's audit log, both environments, newest first. Events are kept for as long as the workspace exists and are deleted with it. next_cursor is present only when another page exists.

workspace_id.description: The workspace id, which is also its live environment's workspace id; the test environment's is the same id with :test appended. A workspace created through the API is tnt_ and a 26-character ULID.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, MAC'd by the server and bound to the workspace it was issued for. Pass it back unchanged as cursor; a tampered, foreign or expired cursor answers 400 invalid_cursor.

type.description: The kind of resource the change acted on.

id.description: The resource's id, when it has one.

AuditEventTargetType.description: The kind of resource the change acted on.

event_id.description: Opaque, workspace-scoped webhook event id. A redelivery of the same event carries the same event_id, so consumers deduplicate on it.

AuthContext.description: Normalised claims from a session your backend has already verified with WorkOS, Clerk, Auth0 or any OIDC provider. Pass the output of the SDK's auth adapters, not a raw token.

provider.description: Lowercase provider slug. WorkOS, Clerk and Auth0 have first-class adapters; every other provider uses a customer-specific OIDC slug. Provider brand is metadata; it does not change risk by itself.

issuer.description: The verified token issuer, normally the provider's HTTPS issuer URL.

audience.description: The verified audience/resource identifier used by the customer's API. Use audiences when the provider emits multiple values.

audiences.description: All verified audience/resource identifiers from an OAuth or OIDC token. The first value may also be copied to audience for simple integrations.

subject.description: The verified stable subject identifier (`sub`), opaque to NoResponse. Required, except from a provider hook at pre_registration, where no user exists yet.

session_id.description: The verified session identifier (`sid` or provider equivalent).

organization_id.description: The active organization or workspace identifier, when the provider issued one.

tenant_id.description: The provider workspace identifier, when distinct from organization_id.

token_id.description: The verified token identifier (`jti`), used for replay and rotation correlation.

session_created_at.description: Creation time of the provider session from the verified backend session record (for example Clerk Session.createdAt or WorkOS Session.created_at). This is separate from token issuance and auth_time.

auth_time.description: Verified end-user authentication time (`auth_time`), when present.

account_created_at.description: Account creation time from the customer's verified provider record, when available.

email_verified.description: Whether the customer's provider asserts that the email identifier was verified.

phone_verified.description: Whether the customer's provider asserts that the phone identifier was verified.

assurance_level.description: Provider or OIDC assurance level, when the customer has mapped one.

impersonated.description: Whether the verified session is acting on behalf of another subject.

transport.description: Where this context was derived. Backend is the trusted integration path; browser values are treated as weak hints. provider_hook is a hosted provider hook (an Auth0 or WorkOS Action) calling at hook_point; it needs hook_point and verified false, and its authentication facts are not scored.

hook_point.description: The provider event a provider_hook context was sent for. pre_registration runs before the user exists, so subject and the request's account_id may be absent there. Sent only with transport provider_hook.

verified.description: Whether the customer completed signature, issuer, audience and expiry validation before calling NoResponse. False contexts are accepted only as weak hints.

mfa.description: Normalized multi-factor evidence from a verified provider session.

roles.description: Bounded role slugs from the verified provider; roles do not change risk by themselves.

scopes.description: Bounded scopes from the verified access token; scopes do not change risk by themselves.

AuthContextMfa.description: Normalized multi-factor evidence from a verified provider session.

AuthenticationErrorCode.description: Machine codes an HTTP 401 answer can carry.

BadRequestErrorCode.description: Machine codes an HTTP 400 answer can carry.

Breach.description: One breach table that matched, detailed view only. name is the catalogue's display name for the table's site, not the upstream provider. No member carries a record, value, password or hash.

domain.description: The breached site's domain, lower case. Absent when the table has none (a credential list, for example).

category.description: The table's category from its name, lower case (social, gaming, combolist, ...).

month.description: Absent when only the year is known.

BreachExposed.description: The kind of data a breach table held beside the identifier. password means a plaintext password was present and password_hash means a hash, salt or token was present. The value itself is not stored or returned; the schema has no member for one.

BreachKind.description: Who is in the table: site_breach, a site's own users; credential_list, a combolist or compilation; stealer_log, malware or botnet victims; scrape; hacking_forum, a criminal hacking, cracking or carding community; abuse_service, the customers of DDoS-for-hire, account generators, dump or card shops, darknet markets, stalkerware or breach-lookup services; darkweb_site, an onion site of unknown purpose.

BreachSelector.description: The submitted email or username whose own search matched the table. A submitted full name is searched as well, and what it finds feeds the identity's reasons rather than this list.

BreachSummary.description: Breach facts for one selector. found is the one required member: false is a definite 'in no breach table'. Every other member is optional, and absent makes no claim. No member carries a breach value, password or hash, and unknown members are refused. truncated means the value matched more tables or records than the lookup keeps, so absence-based claims (a missing name match, for example) are withheld; a truncated result is always found.

breach_count.description: Distinct breach tables the value appears in.

first_year.description: Year of the oldest dated table.

last_year.description: Year of the newest dated table.

exposed.description: The union of data kinds the matching tables held, without the values.

in_credential_lists.description: The value is in a credential_list or stealer_log table.

recent_password_exposure.description: A plaintext password sat next to the value in a table dated two years ago or less, or the value is in a stealer_log table.

Bucket.description: The period each count covers: an hour, or a day or a week (from Monday) in time_zone. Hour buckets are whole UTC hours in any time zone.

Confidence.description: Ordinal confidence in the recommendation under the current policy: low, medium, high or unavailable.

ConflictErrorCode.description: Machine codes an HTTP 409 answer can carry.

Consistency.description: Cross-identifier agreement, computed from facts only. Every member is optional; absent makes no claim.

name.description: The submitted name against breach names and caller-ID names.

phone.description: The submitted phone against numbers found next to the email in breach records.

ip.description: The submitted IP against IPs found next to the email or username in breach records.

country.description: IP country, phone country, breach countries and policy_context.region together.

ConsistencyValue.description: How a submitted identifier agrees with what the evidence holds for the other identifiers. unknown is a definite 'cannot tell' (for example a truncated or too-common breach result); absent means the comparison was not made.

ConsoleLookups.description: The live environment's daily cap on assessments members make through the console (the playground), as spent on the current UTC day. Each console submission with a new Idempotency-Key spends one lookup; a replay spends nothing, and API keys and the test environment spend none. When used reaches limit, the next lookup answers 429 lookup_limit_reached until resets_at. The count is the one the cap enforces.

used.description: Lookups spent since the last reset.

resets_at.description: The next reset: the coming midnight UTC, when used returns to 0.

Country.description: IP country, phone country, breach countries and policy_context.region together.

Coverage.description: Counts only; a zero denominator means no eligible retained records and does not imply a zero rate.

CredentialAssociation.description: An association between an account and an issued key. The response excludes the key and its hash. Retirement removes this association from risk calculations; revoke the actual key through your own service.

account_id.description: Your own opaque identifier for the account being checked, scoped to your workspace. Use an id you mint, with no direct identifier (email, phone, name or national id) in it. '|' is accepted so an Auth0 user id such as 'auth0|64abc' passes unchanged; '@', '+', '$' and whitespace are refused by the pattern, as is an exact-shape JWT; a hex digest such as a SHA-256 is allowed, because hashing an internal id is a common pseudonymous scheme. A value such as '07700900123' or 'jane.doe.gmail.com' cannot be told apart from an opaque id. It travels in bodies, and in a URL only as the path segment of GET /v1/accounts/{account_id} and its /assessments. An assessment requested by a provider hook at pre_registration, which has no account yet, carries the server-issued account_id pre: followed by its assessment_id.

CredentialPage.description: Retained credential associations, ordered by id. Page with the authenticated cursor. Associations are removed on account erasure.

account_id.description: Your own opaque identifier for the account being checked, scoped to your workspace. Use an id you mint, with no direct identifier (email, phone, name or national id) in it. '|' is accepted so an Auth0 user id such as 'auth0|64abc' passes unchanged; '@', '+', '$' and whitespace are refused by the pattern, as is an exact-shape JWT; a hex digest such as a SHA-256 is allowed, because hashing an internal id is a common pseudonymous scheme. A value such as '07700900123' or 'jane.doe.gmail.com' cannot be told apart from an opaque id. It travels in bodies, and in a URL only as the path segment of GET /v1/accounts/{account_id} and its /assessments. An assessment requested by a provider hook at pre_registration, which has no account yet, carries the server-issued account_id pre: followed by its assessment_id.

next_cursor.description: Opaque, expiring cursor bound to this environment, operation and every filter. Keep the filters unchanged.

CredentialRequest.description: Associate the SHA-256 of a high-entropy key issued by your service. Send the hash instead of the key. Repeating a hash returns its original association, including its retirement state. A hash associated with another account returns a conflict.

CustomerExportActionRequest.description: Send an empty JSON object to cancel or retry a customer export.

data.description: Base64-encoded UTF-8 JSON Lines, at most 256 KiB decoded. Each line is a typed customer export record. Decode and concatenate chunks in index order within the same generation.

account_id.description: Your own opaque identifier for the account being checked, scoped to your workspace. Use an id you mint, with no direct identifier (email, phone, name or national id) in it. '|' is accepted so an Auth0 user id such as 'auth0|64abc' passes unchanged; '@', '+', '$' and whitespace are refused by the pattern, as is an exact-shape JWT; a hex digest such as a SHA-256 is allowed, because hashing an internal id is a common pseudonymous scheme. A value such as '07700900123' or 'jane.doe.gmail.com' cannot be told apart from an opaque id. It travels in bodies, and in a URL only as the path segment of GET /v1/accounts/{account_id} and its /assessments. An assessment requested by a provider hook at pre_registration, which has no account yet, carries the server-issued account_id pre: followed by its assessment_id.

Decision.description: An assessment's own decision: block when its stored risk.block is true, otherwise its recommendation. It is not the account's decision or held-admission state.

DecisionReceipt.description: The decision prepared for one HTTP attempt. Its account field preserves the account decision returned for that attempt, even after subsequent changes.

assessment_id.description: Opaque, server-assigned assessment id: 'asm_' and a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID. Unique within the workspace; another workspace's assessment id answers 404.

assessment_version.description: Monotonic revision of this assessment. 1 on the synchronous answer; each material change while the assessment is served (an async continuation settling a source, a change of recommendation, confidence or status) increments it. Expiry does not increment it: an expired assessment is gone, not revised, and the expiry webhook carries the last served version.

policy_version.description: Version of the hand-authored heuristic policy that produced the recommendation, for example 'risk-2026-10.7'. A workspace threshold override adds a +t<N> suffix, e.g. 'risk-2026-10.7+t3'.

Delay.description: How long after the assessment's creation the change was made.

Depth.description: How long the synchronous answer waits for sources. quick waits only for the fast sources, those that answer within 500 ms of ingress (or deadline_ms when lower); full waits for the whole budget, up to 3000 ms. Sources still running at the cut continue asynchronously and update the assessment either way.

endpoint_id.description: Opaque id of the endpoint registration being verified.

challenge.description: Endpoint verification nonce: 32 random bytes, unpadded base64url (43 characters). Fresh per verification.

id.description: The event id, equal to the NR-Webhook-Id header and across redeliveries and every endpoint the event fans out to.

created_at.description: When the event was created. Equal across redeliveries; the signing timestamp header is per delivery.

test.description: Present, and true, only on an event sent by POST /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/test: its data is a fixed example assessment, not one of the workspace's, so a receiver acknowledges it and applies nothing. Real events have no test member.

Enforcement.description: The answer of POST /v1/accounts/{account_id}/enforcements: one enforcement of one of the calling workspace's accounts, kept once per (account, risk_version, flow, action). The first report answers 201 with the new record. A repeat answers 200 with the record as first stored, whatever the repeat's state_before, status, provider or error_code. The one exception is a stored failed record followed by an applied report: the record becomes applied, keeps its id and created_at, takes the applied report's state_before and provider, drops error_code and answers 201, so a successful retry after a failure is recorded. Only an applied record at the account's current risk_version takes the account out of GET /v1/accounts?unenforced=true.

id.description: Opaque, server-assigned id of one recorded enforcement: 'enf_' and 26 Crockford base32 characters. Unique within the workspace.

account_id.description: The account_id of the request path.

risk_version.description: The account's risk_version the workspace acted on. It can be older than the account's current risk_version: such a record is kept and does not count for unenforced.

flow.description: The flow whose decision the workspace acted on.

error_code.description: Why a failed action failed, as a short code of the workspace's choosing (lower-case letters, digits, '_', '.' and '-'), such as the identity provider's error code. Allowed only with status failed: with status applied it answers 400 invalid_request. Keep personal data out of it.

created_at.description: When NoResponse first recorded this enforcement, in UTC. A failed record that becomes applied keeps it.

EnforcementAction.description: What the workspace did in its identity provider: revoke_sessions (signed the account out everywhere), restrict (limited what the account can do), unrestrict (lifted an earlier restriction), fail_onboarding (stopped an account that was still onboarding), reject_activation (refused to activate a provisional account), activate (let a held onboarding or provisional account in) or none (decided to take no action).

EnforcementProvider.description: The identity provider the action ran in; custom for the workspace's own user store.

EnforcementRequest.description: POST /v1/accounts/{account_id}/enforcements body: what the workspace did to the account in its identity provider after reading the account's risk at risk_version. The account is named by the path and the workspace by the API key, so neither is a body member. An enforcement is the workspace's own action, not an outcome: what the workspace later learned about an assessment goes to POST /v1/assessments/{assessment_id}/outcomes. The record's key is (account, risk_version, flow, action), so a retry of the same report is safe and needs no Idempotency-Key.

risk_version.description: The account's risk_version the workspace acted on, as read from GET /v1/accounts/{account_id}, GET /v1/accounts, an assessment answer or account.risk_changed. A version older than the account's current one is accepted and stored; a version newer than the current one answers 409 risk_version_ahead.

flow.description: The flow whose decision (decisions_by_flow) the workspace acted on.

error_code.description: Why a failed action failed, as a short code of the workspace's choosing (lower-case letters, digits, '_', '.' and '-'), such as the identity provider's error code. Allowed only with status failed: with status applied it answers 400 invalid_request. Keep personal data out of it.

EnforcementState.description: The account's state in the workspace's identity provider just before the action: onboarding, provisional (created, not yet activated), active, restricted or rejected.

EnforcementStatus.description: applied when the identity provider accepted the action, failed when it refused it or could not be reached. Only applied counts as enforced.

Enforcements.description: Retained customer enforcement report rows created in [from,to), one row per account/risk_version/flow/action. A later applied report can replace failed at the original created_at; retries are not additional attempts here. applied_coverage divides reported_applied by report rows, including explicit action none; it is not independently verified execution, all requested actions, or prevented fraud. Unreported actions are unknown.

ErasureReceipt.description: Acknowledged propagation of a retained erasure record in the calling environment. Pending means the target has not acknowledged completion. Completion covers these serving-system targets only; backup and point-in-time recovery copies expire according to their own retention policy. This receipt contains no subject id or digest. Workspace teardown revokes customer credentials, so obtain required receipts before teardown.

id.description: Opaque, server-issued erasure receipt id. It contains no subject identifier.

backup_policy.example: Backups expire under the documented backup retention policy.

ExportAssessmentOutcome.description: Structured fields of a retained per-assessment outcome. Legacy notes remain private as promised by the existing outcome contract.

id.description: Opaque, server-assigned id of one recorded outcome: 'out_' and a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID. Unique within the workspace.

assessment_id.description: Opaque, server-assigned assessment id: 'asm_' and a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID. Unique within the workspace; another workspace's assessment id answers 404.

external_ref.description: Your own opaque reference for the outcome, such as a case or ticket id. Stored as given and not interpreted; keep direct identifiers out of it.

Failure.description: Why the attempt failed: the URL is no longer valid, the host did not resolve, it resolved to an address that is not public, no answer within 5 seconds, the connection failed, a 3xx (redirects are not followed) or another non-2xx status. Absent for a delivered attempt.

FailureReason.description: Why a signal or source did not produce a definite found/not_found. timed_out means the source missed the request deadline; a continuation may still settle it. deferred means the (source, identifier) pair is async-only and was not attempted on the synchronous path; a continuation settles it.

Flow.description: The event an assessment is made for: account_creation (a user creates an account), login (a user returns to an existing account) or purchase (a payment or a credit grant). The account's risk is reported with the decision for this flow.

FlowChange.description: A change to one flow. A field left out keeps the value in force. Thresholds set on login or purchase start from the values in force, account_creation's while it inherits them. After the change, 0 < step_up < review <= 100 and block is off or review <= block <= 100.

block.description: The score from which the decision is block; null turns blocking off.

inherits_account_creation.description: Login or purchase only: drop the flow's own thresholds so it uses account_creation's again. Not combined with step_up, review or block. Send true; false is refused.

inherits_signup.description: Alias of inherits_account_creation, still accepted. Send true; false is refused.

hold_seconds.description: How long a held flow's assessment is held after it was created, 30 to 86400 seconds (default 300). Kept while the flow is immediate.

FlowSettings.description: One flow's policy in force. A score below step_up is allow, below review step_up, and from review review; from block, when present, the decision is block. admission says when the flow's decision is final.

block.description: The score from which the decision is block. Absent while blocking is off, the default.

default_depth.description: The depth a request for this flow that names none is served at. Defaults: full for account_creation and purchase, quick for login.

inherits_account_creation.description: true while this flow has no thresholds of its own and uses account_creation's, the default for login and purchase. Always false for signup.

hold_seconds.description: How long a held flow's assessment is held after it was created, 30 to 86400 seconds (default 300). Kept while the flow is immediate.

Footprint.description: How long and how widely the signup's email and username have existed, and how far independent sources agree on the person behind them, in years and counts only. families are the kinds of evidence that found either identifier. Omitted when nothing found them: a footprint lookup that failed makes no claim, and absence is no_digital_footprint's to state.

FootprintFamily.description: The source-neutral kind of evidence: account_presence (an account found on a site), auth_provider (the account at your auth provider), breach (breach and credential tables), breach_abuse (abuse and fraud communities' tables) and code_hosting (a code hosting profile).

FootprintTimeline.description: One identifier's dated footprint across every source: the first and last year any event was seen, the years between them, the latest year a source dated activity (omitted when none did), how many distinct sites and which kinds of evidence saw it.

Freshness.description: Freshness class of the evidence behind a signal. unknown whenever no evidence was obtained.

HookPoint.description: The provider event a provider_hook context was sent for; absent for any other transport.

IdentifierKind.description: Which submitted identifier a signal concerns. ip is a selector of breach_exposure only.

Impact.description: The selected reason's served impact band. Requires reason.

IncompleteReason.description: Why a lane did not settle. deferred means the lane is asynchronous and still running; a continuation settles it. timed_out means the lane missed its deadline. insufficient_evidence is a settled inconclusive signal rather than an incomplete lane.

IncompleteSource.description: One evidence lane that did not settle, and why. It names a lane, not a source. A lane that missed its deadline is timed_out rather than not_found.

Integration.description: A hosted provider integration. Point the provider at url: a WorkOS user registration or authentication Action, or the NoResponse Auth0 Action, which sends secret as a bearer token. The answer allows or denies the event: deny only when the assessment's risk.block is true, and allow on every failure, so a fault on the NoResponse side lets the user through. secret is present only in the answers of POST /v1/integrations and POST /v1/integrations/{integration_id}/rotate for an Auth0 integration, and is not returned again.

integration_id.description: Opaque, server-assigned integration id: int_ and a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID. Another workspace's integration id answers 404.

hook_points.description: Each hook point at most once.

secret.description: Auth0 only, and only when it is created or rotated: the shared secret the Auth0 Action sends as Authorization: Bearer <secret>. nri_ and 43 unpadded base64url characters (32 random bytes). Store it as an Auth0 Action secret.

rotated_at.description: When the secret was last rotated; absent until the first rotation.

previous_secret_expires_at.description: After a rotation, when the replaced secret stops being accepted; absent when no replaced secret is still accepted.

IntegrationHookPoint.description: pre_registration runs before the user exists; post_login runs after a successful sign-in.

IntegrationList.description: GET /v1/integrations: every integration of the workspace, oldest first, at most 10. No secret is ever listed.

IntegrationPlatform.description: The authentication provider that calls the endpoint.

IntegrationRequest.description: POST /v1/integrations body. Registers a hosted endpoint for one authentication provider. The workspace is the API key that signs the request, so the body has no workspace field and refuses one like any other unknown member. A WorkOS integration needs signing_secret, the Actions secret shown in the WorkOS dashboard, which NoResponse uses to verify each Action request and to sign its answer. A Supabase integration needs signing_secret, the hook secret Supabase generates for a Before User Created HTTPS hook (v1,whsec_ and base64), which NoResponse uses to verify each call. An Auth0 integration sends no signing_secret: NoResponse generates the shared secret and returns it once.

hook_points.description: The provider events the endpoint scores. Default every hook point the platform has: pre_registration (WorkOS user registration Action, Auth0 pre-user-registration trigger, Supabase Before User Created hook) and post_login (WorkOS authentication Action, Auth0 post-login trigger). Supabase has only pre_registration, so a Supabase integration that lists post_login is refused. An event that is not listed is answered allow without an assessment.

signing_secret.description: The WorkOS Actions signing secret or the Supabase hook secret, as the provider's dashboard shows it: 16 to 256 printable ASCII characters with no spaces. It is stored sealed and is not returned.

IntegrationRotationRequest.description: POST /v1/integrations/{integration_id}/rotate body. For an Auth0 integration send {}: NoResponse generates a new shared secret and returns it once. For a WorkOS or Supabase integration send the new signing_secret after regenerating it in the provider's dashboard. Either way the previous secret is still accepted for 24 hours, so the provider can be switched over without a refused call.

signing_secret.description: The WorkOS Actions signing secret or the Supabase hook secret, as the provider's dashboard shows it: 16 to 256 printable ASCII characters with no spaces. It is stored sealed and is not returned.

Invite.description: A pending workspace invitation. Creating or reissuing it returns a token once; lists omit it. The token can be accepted once before expiry and is invalidated on revocation or reissue. Token state does not establish email delivery.

id.description: Opaque, server-assigned invite id: inv_ and a 26-character ULID.

workspace_id.description: The workspace id, which is also its live environment's workspace id; the test environment's is the same id with :test appended. A workspace created through the API is tnt_ and a 26-character ULID.

email.description: Where the console sends the invite. Informational: it is not matched against the accepting user.

external_user_id.description: The user's id at the identity provider the console signs people in with: 1 to 256 printable ASCII characters with no space, compared exactly.

created_by.description: The stable member id that issued this invite, or the authenticated live API key prefix for members_manage automation. Reissuing preserves the original creator; the audit event names the reissuing actor.

token.description: The invite token: nrinv_, the invite id's ULID, _ and 43 unpadded base64url characters (32 random bytes). The new member's console sends it to POST /v1/invites/accept.

environments.description: Allowed data environments. Invites default to both. Omitted on member PATCH preserves the current grants; owners retain both.

denied_actions.description: Independent removals from a built-in preset: sensitive evidence, exports, or active policy publication. Owners retain full authority. Omitted member updates preserve exclusions.

reissued_at.description: Last token reissue, not proof of email delivery.

InviteList.description: GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/invites: the workspace's pending invites, oldest first, at most 50, with no token.

InviteRequest.description: POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/invites body. Creates an invite for role and returns its token once. email is where the console sends the token and is not checked against the user who accepts. With external_user_id set, only that user can accept.

email.description: Where the console sends the invite. Informational: it is not matched against the accepting user.

external_user_id.description: The user's id at the identity provider the console signs people in with: 1 to 256 printable ASCII characters with no space, compared exactly.

environments.description: Allowed data environments. Invites default to both. Omitted on member PATCH preserves the current grants; owners retain both.

denied_actions.description: Independent removals from a built-in preset: sensitive evidence, exports, or active policy publication. Owners retain full authority. Omitted member updates preserve exclusions.

IpSummary.description: Facts about the submitted IP from the offline database and this workspace's own recent assessments. Every member is optional; absent makes no claim.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the address.

asn.description: Autonomous system number of the network that announces the address, from the offline database. Absent when unknown.

seen_in_workspace.description: Assessments in this workspace with the same IP in the last 24 hours, this one included. A count only.

Key.description: One API key of your workspace. A key belongs to exactly one environment. key, the secret credential, is present only in the answer that created the key: NoResponse keeps a peppered digest of it, so store it now. Every other field is safe to show.

id.description: The key's public id, a 26-character ULID.

workspace_id.description: The workspace id, which is also its live environment's workspace id; the test environment's is the same id with :test appended. A workspace created through the API is tnt_ and a 26-character ULID.

prefix.description: The public start of the credential, nrk_<environment>_<key id>, which identifies the key in logs and secret stores without its secret.

scopes.description: The key's scopes, each at most once.

status.description: active: the key authenticates. expired: a rotation's overlap window has ended (expires_at). revoked: the key was revoked (revoked_at) and answers 401.

created_by.description: The external user id of the member who created the key through the console, or the prefix (nrk_<environment>_<key id>) of the management key that created it. Absent for a key NoResponse issued or a rotation made.

expires_at.description: The earlier of the explicit lifetime and any rotation overlap. Rotation preserves the original lifetime.

revoked_by.description: The external user id of the member who revoked the key through the console, or the prefix of the management key that revoked it. Absent when the key is not revoked or NoResponse revoked it.

key.description: The credential, nrk_<environment>_<key id>_<secret>. Present only in the 201 answer that created the key.

name.description: The optional display name supplied for this API key. Preserved on rotation.

purpose.description: Optional operational purpose, at most 200 printable characters without leading or trailing whitespace. Do not put secrets or personal data here. Preserved on rotation and included in the creation request fingerprint; omitted for older credentials.

owner_user_id.description: The issuing member's external identity for a personal key. Personal ownership is fixed and the key is revoked when that member loses authority. Service keys belong to the workspace and omit this field.

rotated_to.description: Replacement public key identifier, or legacy when the successor predates recorded lineage. This field excludes the secret.

last_used_at.description: Latest recorded authenticated request observation, updated at most once per minute. Capture is best effort after the response and includes authenticated requests refused by authorization or rate limits. Absence means unknown and does not prove the key was unused. It is independent of diagnostic retention and resets on the replacement key after rotation. This field retains no raw IP or user-agent.

key_id.description: The public id of the workspace API key that made the change.

KeyEnvironment.description: The environment the key belongs to. A live key assesses with live sources; a test key answers from the deterministic simulator.

KeyList.description: GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/keys: the keys of both of the workspace's environments, newest first, at most 200 of each, revoked and expired keys included. No item carries a secret.

KeyRequest.description: Creates a key whose scopes are bounded by the issuer capabilities in this environment. Delete is owner-only. A service key outlives its creator; a personal key belongs to the authenticated member and is revoked on membership or authority changes. request_id deduplicates creation: retry returns 200 metadata without the secret; changed parameters answer 409. Team scopes members and members_manage are explicitly workspace-wide, live-only, and delegated by a current full owner. Personal credentials cannot hold management or members_manage. Legacy management includes policy publication; use settings without policy_publish for configuration preparation and retention-only edits.

scopes.description: The key's scopes, each at most once.

name.description: Optional display name for this API key, at most 100 printable characters. Preserved on rotation.

purpose.description: Optional operational purpose, at most 200 printable characters without leading or trailing whitespace. Do not put secrets or personal data here. Preserved on rotation and included in the creation request fingerprint; omitted for older credentials.

expires_at.description: Between one minute and 365 days from now.

request_id.description: Caller-chosen identifier for one creation attempt, scoped to the issuing actor and environment. Use 1 to 256 printable ASCII characters without spaces. A retry with the same parameters returns the original key metadata with status 200 and no secret; changed parameters return 409.

KeyRotation.description: The 201 answer of POST /v1/keys/rotate: the new key, shown once, and when the key that was presented stops working. The new key has the scopes and the environment of the presented key.

key.description: The new credential, nrk_<mode>_<key id>_<secret>, in the environment of the presented key: nrk_live_ or nrk_test_. It is shown only in this answer; store it now.

key_id.description: The public id of the new key.

scopes.description: The scopes of the new key: those of the presented key.

previous_key_id.description: The id of the key that signed this request.

previous_key_expires_at.description: When the previous key stops authenticating. Until then both keys work.

KeyRotationRequest.description: POST /v1/keys/rotate body. The workspace and the key being rotated are the API key that signs the request, so neither is a body member. An empty object takes the default overlap.

overlap_seconds.description: How long the presented key keeps working beside the new one, from 60 seconds to 7 days. Default 86400 (24 hours). At the end of the overlap the presented key stops authenticating.

KeyStatus.description: active: the key authenticates. expired: a rotation's overlap window has ended (expires_at). revoked: the key was revoked (revoked_at) and answers 401.

KeyUsageBatch.description: The 202 answer of POST /v1/key_usage/batches. A replay with the same Idempotency-Key and body answers the same record and counts nothing again.

id.description: Opaque, server-assigned id of the batch: 'kub_' and a 26-character Crockford base32 ULID.

received_at.description: When NoResponse first recorded the batch.

ignored.description: Events that added nothing: a private, reserved or unreadable ip, or an occurred_at more than 24 hours old or more than 5 minutes ahead.

KeyUsageBatchRequest.description: POST /v1/key_usage/batches body: facts about requests made with API keys your platform issued to your accounts, one event per request. Each event names the key by the SHA-256 that the assessment's issued_credential.sha256 carried, not the key itself. The SDKs buffer events and send them in the background. A batch holds 1 to 500 events and at most 256 KiB. Idempotency-Key is required and binds the body as on POST /v1/assessments, so a retried batch is counted once.

KeyUsageEvent.description: One request made with an issued key. An event whose ip is not a public address, or whose occurred_at is more than 24 hours old or more than 5 minutes ahead, is counted in ignored and adds nothing.

key_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the issued key's UTF-8 bytes, as 64 lower-case hex characters: the value sent as issued_credential.sha256 when the account was assessed. Each SDK's issued-credential helper computes it.

ip.description: The client IP address the request came from, IPv4 or IPv6, as your server saw it. Stored only as a keyed digest and its country.

user_agent.description: The request's User-Agent header, at most 512 characters. Stored only as a keyed digest.

model.description: The model or product the request used, such as gpt-4o-mini. Stored only as a keyed digest.

sample_rate.description: The share of requests your sampler records, when it records only some: 0.1 means this event stands for 10 requests. Request and token totals are weighted by its inverse. Distinct IP and country counts see only the events sent.

Lane.description: An evidence lane: accounts (account presence for email and username), phone, breach, domain (the email domain's registration) and ip.

ListBulkRequest.description: At most 100 additions and removals combined. One transaction applies all changes or none. Idempotency-Key prevents duplicate changes for 24 hours; a different body under the same key returns 409. Matching reads see the new list immediately, while bounded durable jobs propagate account risk notifications.

ListChange.description: A committed bulk list change and bounded notification progress, available while propagation is pending and for 24 hours after all propagation completes. References count an account once per changed list entry and are not unique accounts. No endpoint delivery or customer enforcement is implied by completed.

ListEntry.description: One entry of an environment's list: an exact email or an email domain that decides an account whatever its score. An account matches when one of its admitted assessments sent the email, or an email of the domain. A block entry decides block for every flow and an allow entry decides allow; when both match, block wins. The account's risk carries the list_match reason with the entry's id, and its score stays the one the assessment's facts give. A held flow still waits for its investigation.

id.description: The entry's id: lst_ and a ULID.

workspace_id.description: The workspace id, which is also its live environment's workspace id; the test environment's is the same id with :test appended. A workspace created through the API is tnt_ and a 26-character ULID.

value.description: The value the entry matches, in canonical form: an email lower-cased whole, or a domain lower-cased and taken to its registrable domain (mail.example.co.uk is stored as example.co.uk).

note.description: Why the entry exists, for the people who manage the list. It is shown with the entry and decides nothing.

created_by.description: The external user id of the member who added the entry through the console, or the prefix (nrk_<environment>_<key id>) of the management key that added it.

expires_at.description: Optional expiry. An expired entry stops matching immediately; bounded maintenance removes it and propagates account risk changes.

ListEntryAction.description: block decides block for the accounts the entry matches; allow decides allow. Block wins when both match.

ListEntryKind.description: email matches one address, whatever the case of its local part. email_domain matches every address of the registrable domain and of its subdomains.

ListEntryList.description: Newest first. Without a query, returns every active entry for compatibility. With limit or cursor, returns up to 100 entries and an authenticated workspace/environment-bound cursor. Expired entries are omitted.

ListEntryRequest.description: POST /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/lists/{environment} body. Adds one entry to the environment's list and, in the same change, re-decides every account it matches: each sends account.risk_changed when a decision changes. Needs the admin or owner role, or a management key of the environment.

value.description: An email address for kind email, written as in an assessment request; an LDH domain (A-label for an internationalised one) such as example.com for kind email_domain, which must sit below a public suffix (co.uk alone is refused with 400). NoResponse stores it in canonical form and answers that form.

note.description: Why the entry exists, for the people who manage the list. It is shown with the entry and decides nothing.

expires_at.description: Optional expiry. An expired entry stops matching immediately; bounded maintenance removes it and propagates account risk changes.

ListImpact.description: List override changes among the newest 5000 matching accounts. These counts describe override inputs. Customer enforcement and eventual outcomes remain separate. The response reports whether the matching population was truncated.

ListMatch.description: The list action captured at the first answer. Requires revision first. Older answers without captured list state do not match, including none.

ListPreviewRequest.description: Choose an addition or a removal. The preview performs no list, account, audit, outcome or outbox write.

Member.description: One member of a workspace: an external user id holding one role. A removed member loses every permission at once.

id.description: Opaque, server-assigned member id: mem_ and a 26-character ULID. It stays the same when a removed member is invited back.

workspace_id.description: The workspace id, which is also its live environment's workspace id; the test environment's is the same id with :test appended. A workspace created through the API is tnt_ and a 26-character ULID.

external_user_id.description: The user's id at the identity provider the console signs people in with: 1 to 256 printable ASCII characters with no space, compared exactly.

status.description: Listed and returned members are active.

environments.description: Allowed data environments. Invites default to both. Omitted on member PATCH preserves the current grants; owners retain both.

denied_actions.description: Independent removals from a built-in preset: sensitive evidence, exports, or active policy publication. Owners retain full authority. Omitted member updates preserve exclusions.

principal_id.description: Immutable internal workspace principal, equal to member id, preserved across explicit provider-identity migrations.

display_name.description: Informational display name. Authentication and provider identity use the verified subject binding.

unverified_email.description: Unverified contact address for display. Empty clears it; a supplied value must be an address. Identity linking uses the verified provider subject.

MemberList.description: GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/members: the workspace's active members, oldest first, at most 100.

MemberStatus.description: Listed and returned members are active.

MemberUpdateRequest.description: PATCH /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/members/{member_id} body: the member's new role. The workspace's last owner cannot be demoted.

environments.description: Allowed data environments. Invites default to both. Omitted on member PATCH preserves the current grants; owners retain both.

denied_actions.description: Independent removals from a built-in preset: sensitive evidence, exports, or active policy publication. Owners retain full authority. Omitted member updates preserve exclusions.

Metric.description: assessments: assessments admitted. webhook_deliveries: events sent to endpoints, one per event per endpoint. key_usage_events: key-usage events accepted.

NotFoundErrorCode.description: Machine codes an HTTP 404 answer can carry.

OnExpiry.description: The decision a held assessment takes when hold_seconds pass before its investigation completes, unless the evidence so far gives a stricter one (default review). It is announced as account.risk_changed like any other change, so an expired hold is always announced. A hosted provider hook, which cannot wait, answers a held account by it at once: deny for block, allow otherwise. Kept while the flow is immediate.

OperationalAggregate.description: One repeatable-read snapshot of retained request diagnostics or webhook attempts. Capture can have gaps and these counts are not a billing ledger. Unattributed keys include older requests and member requests. Queue state is current retained work, not a delivery success denominator.

buckets.description: Nonempty UTC buckets in ascending order. Counts include all retained matching attempts, without the log page limit.

queue.description: Current retained delivery queue, independent of the requested attempt window and status filter. Endpoint filter applies. Does not prove customer enforcement execution.

p50_ms.description: Continuous percentile over retained attempts. Omitted when there are no captured samples.

p95_ms.description: Continuous percentile over retained attempts. Omitted when there are no captured samples.

p99_ms.description: Continuous percentile over retained attempts. Omitted when there are no captured samples.

p99_ms.description: Continuous percentile over retained attempts. Omitted when there are no captured samples.

Outcome.description: What the provider later learned about the assessed account. confirmed_abuse, account_takeover and chargeback report abuse; false_positive and legitimate withdraw an earlier abuse report of this workspace for the assessment; unknown is recorded only. Outcomes are append-only and the latest one recorded for an assessment wins.

by_outcome.description: Current customer-reported labels, not independently established ground truth. Missing keys mean zero. Unknown is an explicit report; absent or expired feedback is unreported.

Outcomes.description: Accounts whose current completed assessment was created in the selected window and remains retained at as_of. The effective account feedback head is observed at as_of, including explicit unknown reports. Customer-reported labels and unlabelled accounts have separate counts. Superseded labels are excluded.

OutcomesByOutcome.description: Current customer-reported labels, not independently established ground truth. Missing keys mean zero. Unknown is an explicit report; absent or expired feedback is unreported.

OwnerType.description: The credential namespace of the creator. An external user ID equal to an API-key label does not grant ownership of that key's private view.

PermissionDeniedErrorCode.description: Machine codes an HTTP 403 answer can carry.

PhoneEnrichment.description: Facts about the number only: line type, carrier and country. The upstream provider, its scores and its verdicts stay internal.

Platform.description: Client platform. Closed vocabulary keeps integrations stable.

change_reason.example: Reviewed the proposal and its capture coverage.

label_collection.example: Customer support reviewed the outcome labels for the selected cohort.

PolicyHistory.description: Immutable settings snapshots, newest first. history_complete is false when earlier versions predate capture. A restored version is published with a fresh version number. History is removed with the tenant.

recorded_at.description: Capture time, not a backfilled activation time. Absent only for the current configuration before its first capture.

PolicyPreview.description: Exact threshold transitions among eligible retained first answers, newest first within the limit. Partial older revisions without a frozen hold snapshot are reported as unsupported. Preview leaves account state, outcomes and source evidence unchanged.

historical_population_known.description: Deleted, expired and uncaptured records cannot be reconstructed. Counts describe retained evidence and provide no causal estimate of fraud prevented.

PolicyPreviewRequest.description: Side-effect-free threshold preview for at most 31 days. Retained first answers are evaluated at their exact frozen scores using the production threshold and hold rules. Changes to admission, source selection, depth or retention are not simulated.

PolicyRestoreRequest.description: Publish a captured configuration as a new version. Version checks and publication are atomic. Longer retention does not revive expired records, and restored policy does not undo customer enforcement.

Population.description: first_answers uses anonymous counters that can include erased detail. retained_first_answers computes exact intersections over retained first answers within 31 days. Requests exceeding the 100000-record work budget are refused.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem document returned by every error response, with a stable machine code and the request id.

detail.example: identifiers: at least one of email, username or phone is required.

reason.example: at least one of email, username or phone is required

Publication.description: Immutable publication provenance remains in policy history after evaluation evidence expires. SHA-256 values identify the frozen manifest, evaluator semantic input, cohort, and canonical result separately.

RateLimitErrorCode.description: Machine codes an HTTP 429 answer can carry.

ReasonCode.description: A stable reason code. New codes may appear; ignore any you do not know.

ReasonIdentifier.description: The submitted identifier or client context field a reason concerns; absent when it concerns the whole assessment. Client context is a claimed hint, not a device fingerprint.

Recommendation.description: The recommended action: allow, step_up or review. Your application applies it.

RequestAggregateRequest.description: Count every retained matching attempt in [from,to). Capture is best effort; missing attempts cannot be inferred. UTC buckets may be partial at the edges. The window is at most 7 days.

RequestDiagnostic.description: One authenticated HTTP attempt. An attempt id is independent of the caller correlation id. No raw body, path parameter, credential or source payload is retained. write_complete means the server wrote/flushed its response, not proof the client processed it. Collection is bounded best effort; ii_signup_request_diagnostic_failures_total exposes gaps. Retained for seven days or the shorter environment retention.

api_key_id.description: Public authenticated API key identifier. Absent for member requests and older unattributed diagnostics.

RequestDiagnosticPage.description: Authenticated attempts in a bounded interval, newest first. Keep the same filters when paging.

note.example: Reviewed the retained account evidence and customer report.

ResponseMode.description: standard returns the consolidated risk response; detailed adds merged provider-neutral facts when the key has detailed scope. There is no raw mode.

account_id.description: Your own opaque identifier for the account being checked, scoped to your workspace. Use an id you mint, with no direct identifier (email, phone, name or national id) in it. '|' is accepted so an Auth0 user id such as 'auth0|64abc' passes unchanged; '@', '+', '$' and whitespace are refused by the pattern, as is an exact-shape JWT; a hex digest such as a SHA-256 is allowed, because hashing an internal id is a common pseudonymous scheme. A value such as '07700900123' or 'jane.doe.gmail.com' cannot be told apart from an opaque id. It travels in bodies, and in a URL only as the path segment of GET /v1/accounts/{account_id} and its /assessments. An assessment requested by a provider hook at pre_registration, which has no account yet, carries the server-issued account_id pre: followed by its assessment_id.

assignee_principal_id.description: Immutable workspace member ID. assignee is the historical display identity captured at assignment.

ReviewSubject.description: A tenant-local investigation link. risk_version is the account risk version captured when the link was added. It does not assert a relationship or change feedback or enforcement.

reason.example: Linked during review of the account evidence.

ReviewSubjectRequest.description: An assessment link also requires assessment_id and assessment_version; an issued_credential link also requires credential_id. Every reference must belong to account_id in this environment. Other kinds reject those fields.

owner_type.description: The credential namespace of the creator. An external user ID equal to an API-key label does not grant ownership of that key's private view.

owner_principal_id.description: Immutable member ID or API key ID, interpreted with owner_type. Ownership survives changes to an external user identity.

conclusions.description: Current resolution of each resolved retained review; prior resolutions and reopened reviews do not count. Missing keys mean zero. These investigation conclusions are independent of account feedback.

Reviews.description: Reviews created in [from,to) whose review and current account assessment remain retained. Status and assignment are current at as_of, not a transition history. label_coverage numerator is resolved reviews labeled benign or abuse; denominator is resolved reviews. Inconclusive is not a known outcome. Review conclusions do not change account feedback or enforcement.

ReviewsConclusions.description: Current resolution of each resolved retained review; prior resolutions and reopened reviews do not count. Missing keys mean zero. These investigation conclusions are independent of account feedback.

Risk.description: The one risk decision for this event. score is 0 (safe) to 100 (risky), set by the reasons that fired under a hand-set, versioned heuristic policy. Each reason carries its direction and impact band; the policy's weights are not published. Every answer with a recommendation carries it, and the top-level recommendation equals risk.recommendation. It names no source or provider.

block.description: true when the workspace's block threshold is set and score reached it. A provider hook can deny the account creation on it; the provider decides and enforces. It does not change recommendation. It is false while blocking is off, the default, and a body from before the flag existed omits it: read absent as false.

block_threshold.description: The block threshold this answer used: block is true exactly when score is at least this value. Absent while blocking is off. NoResponse sets it per workspace on request, at or above the review threshold.

confidence.description: How much of the planned evidence answered; it says nothing about risk.

policy_version.description: Version of the hand-authored heuristic policy that produced the recommendation, for example 'risk-2026-10.7'. A workspace threshold override adds a +t<N> suffix, e.g. 'risk-2026-10.7+t3'.

policy_basis.description: Labels the v0 policy as hand-authored and not statistically validated.

reasons.description: Every reason that fired: risk-raising reasons first, then neutral, then risk-lowering, each strongest impact band first and then by code. The policy's numeric weights are kept private, so a reason carries only its direction and impact band.

summary.description: A few typed facts per identifier. Every fact is optional: absent means the evidence did not answer and makes no claim, while false or 0 is a definite answer. Lanes that do not exist yet leave their members absent.

coverage.description: Sources counted by state, not named.

details.description: Detailed view only (response_mode=detailed, which needs the detailed scope); a standard answer leaves it out. Merged observations without provider, source, origin, raw breach record, value or score.

RiskConfidence.description: How much of the planned evidence answered; it says nothing about risk.

RiskCoverage.description: Sources counted by state, not named.

answered.description: Sources that gave a definite answer.

RiskDetails.description: Detailed view only (response_mode=detailed, which needs the detailed scope); a standard answer leaves it out. Merged observations without provider, source, origin, raw breach record, value or score.

breaches.description: The matching breach tables, newest first, at most 100.

breach_names.description: Names found next to the identifiers in breach records, merged, with the number of distinct tables each was seen in and the sites of those tables.

events.description: The identity's dated footprint events, newest first, at most 300: the year and month, what happened (created, last_active, breached), the site, its category, the kind of evidence and the identifier it belongs to. No breach value: dates are coarsened to the month.

sites.description: The domains of the breached sites whose tables hold the name, lower case, each once, newest breach first, at most 32: the domain values of breaches[]. Covers the email's and the username's tables together. Absent when none of the tables has a site.

unsited.description: How many of the tables that hold the name have no site, such as a credential list or a stealer log. Absent when none.

RiskReason.description: One reason that fired. direction is whether it raises or lowers the score, or is neutral (informational, it moves nothing). impact is a coarse band of how much it moves the score: none for a neutral reason, otherwise low, medium or high.

code.description: A stable reason code. New codes may appear; ignore any you do not know.

list_entry_id.description: The list entry a list_match reason applied. No other reason carries it.

RiskSummary.description: A few typed facts per identifier. Every fact is optional: absent means the evidence did not answer and makes no claim, while false or 0 is a definite answer. Lanes that do not exist yet leave their members absent.

breach.description: Breach facts for the email. Replaces the boolean breached.

report_count.description: Highest report count any source gave for the number.

carrier.description: Carrier-network metadata from privately weighted sources; not upstream provider attribution.

Role.description: A built-in capability set. Specialist roles are independent; effective access is returned by GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/capabilities.

SentIdentifiers.description: The identifiers an assessment was sent: each member of the request's identifiers object exactly as received, before the server normalised it (the email domain keeps its case, the name its Unicode form). A member the request did not send is absent. NoResponse keeps them encrypted under the workspace's own key, does not index or log them, and deletes them with the assessment: on DELETE of the assessment or its account, at its expires_at, and with the workspace.

email.description: identifiers.email as the request sent it.

username.description: identifiers.username as the request sent it.

phone.description: identifiers.phone as the request sent it.

name.description: identifiers.name as the request sent it, before NFC normalisation.

ip.description: identifiers.ip as the request sent it.

Settings.description: One environment's settings: how long its assessments are kept, and for each flow the risk thresholds that decide it and the depth a request that names none is served at, and the sources it refuses. Live and test each have their own. A flow without thresholds of its own uses account_creation's (inherits_account_creation). Every change is recorded in the audit log as settings.updated, with who made it.

workspace_id.description: The workspace id, which is also its live environment's workspace id; the test environment's is the same id with :test appended. A workspace created through the API is tnt_ and a 26-character ULID.

retention_days.description: Days an assessment is kept after it is created, 1 to 365 (default 365). Shortening hides older assessments at once.

policy_version.description: The monotonic settings configuration epoch, including retention changes. Zero while defaults apply. Historical assessments keep their frozen policy version; the active version reaches new assessments within a minute.

updated_by.description: Who last changed the policy: the member's external user id for a change made through the console, the prefix (nrk_<environment>_<key id>) of the management key that made it, or NoResponse. Absent while the defaults apply.

updated_at.description: When the policy last changed. Absent while the defaults apply.

refused_sources.description: The sources this environment refuses, sorted; empty, the default, refuses none. An assessment leaves a refused source out: its coverage is missing (an identifier with no other source lists coverage-unavailable as unavailable) rather than not_found, and a stored result of a refused source is not reused.

SettingsRequest.description: Changes only named settings, atomically. Every successful write advances policy_version and retains an immutable settings snapshot. expected_policy_version optionally guards against stale edits; restore always requires it.

refused_sources.description: Replaces the refused sources; [] refuses none. A change applies to new assessments within a minute.

flows.description: Use account_creation or its deprecated alias signup, not both.

expected_policy_version.description: Compare-and-set guard. A stale version returns 409 policy_version_conflict before any change; every settings write including retention advances the version.

type.description: Signal kind, for example account_presence or breach_exposure. New kinds may appear; ignore any you do not know.

source_id.description: Opaque, workspace-scoped projection of the source that produced a signal. It stays stable for your workspace while the projection key is unchanged and reveals no upstream provider, feed, breach table or source record.

evidence_ref.description: Opaque pointer to evidence NoResponse holds for this signal. It carries no breach value, credential or page body.

observed_at.description: When the evidence was first observed.

last_checked_at.description: When the source was last queried for this identifier.

enrichment.description: Only present for a found phone signal. Curated facts about the number, without raw upstream documents or the provider's identity, scores or verdicts; follows normal record retention and deletion.

SignalOutcome.description: Per-signal outcome. A source that timed out, was blocked or errored reports blocked, unavailable or inconclusive with a reason and is listed in incomplete_sources; not_found is a definite absence.

SigningKey.description: One signing key, by id. The secret is not included.

key_id.description: The signing key id, sent as NR-Webhook-Key-Id on every delivery it signs.

expires_at.description: Present on a key a rotation replaced: it stops verifying at this instant, 7 days after the rotation. Absent on the key that signs.

SigningSecret.description: A newly issued signing key with its secret, shown only in this answer. A receiver verifies NR-Webhook-Signature with the secret's UTF-8 bytes as the HMAC-SHA256 key.

key_id.description: The signing key id, sent as NR-Webhook-Key-Id on every delivery it signs.

secret.description: The signing secret: 32 random bytes as 43 characters of unpadded base64url. It is not stored in readable form or returned again.

SourceId.description: A NoResponse source: github (GitHub accounts), phone (the phone lookup), breach (breach exposure), rdap (the email domain's registration), mx (the email domain's mail servers) or ipintel (IP intelligence).

Status.description: complete: final; nothing is still running. A lane that failed or missed its 10 s deadline stays listed in incomplete_sources, and confidence is lower. partial: a recommendation exists and at least one lane is still running or did not settle (see incomplete_sources). pending: nothing usable before the deadline; no recommendation yet, poll or wait for the webhook.

Transport.description: Where the context was derived: backend (also when the request named no transport), browser, or provider_hook for a hosted provider hook.

Usage.description: Body of the 200 answer to GET /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/usage: what the workspace's environments were metered for on each UTC day from from through to. Each billable unit is counted once, where it becomes final: an assessment when it is admitted (by flow and depth), a webhook delivery once per event per endpoint (retries and replays add nothing), and a key-usage event once when the ingest accepts it. A count does not change when the assessment, account or workspace is later deleted. A day, environment or metric with nothing counted has no item. No prices or billing. console_lookups is the one limit: the live environment's daily cap on console lookups, as spent today.

workspace_id.description: The workspace id, which is also its live environment's workspace id; the test environment's is the same id with :test appended. A workspace created through the API is tnt_ and a 26-character ULID.

to.description: The last UTC day covered, included.

items.description: Ordered by environment (live first), then day, metric, flow and depth.

console_lookups.description: Present when the caller may read the live environment (a member allowed live, or a live key with the usage scope) and the API enforces the console lookup cap. Absent otherwise; it does not depend on from and to.

metric.description: assessments: assessments admitted. webhook_deliveries: events sent to endpoints, one per event per endpoint. key_usage_events: key-usage events accepted.

external_user_id.description: The user's id at the identity provider the console signs people in with: 1 to 256 printable ASCII characters with no space, compared exactly.

console_credential_id.description: The public id of the console credential the user acted through.

principal_id.description: Stable workspace principal id, retained across identity-provider subject migration. Absent for older events.

WebhookAggregateRequest.description: Count every retained matching attempt in [from,to). Capture is best effort; missing attempts cannot be inferred. UTC buckets may be partial at the edges. The window is at most 30 days.

endpoint_id.description: Opaque id of the endpoint registration.

event_id.description: The event id the receiver saw as NR-Webhook-Id and as the body's id. Replay it with POST /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/deliveries/{event_id}/replay.

event_type.description: The event's type, as its body's type: assessment.updated, endpoint.verification, account.deleted, workspace.deleted, webhook_endpoint.disabled, account.risk_changed, audit.event, or a type added later.

attempt.description: Which attempt of this delivery this was: 1 for the first send, up to 9 with retries. A replay counts its own attempts from 1.

replay.description: true for an attempt of a replay you asked for.

status.description: delivered when the endpoint answered 2xx; failed otherwise, with failure naming why.

response_code.description: The HTTP status the endpoint answered. Absent when no response was read.

failure.description: Why the attempt failed: the URL is no longer valid, the host did not resolve, it resolved to an address that is not public, no answer within 5 seconds, the connection failed, a 3xx (redirects are not followed) or another non-2xx status. Absent for a delivered attempt.

latency_ms.description: Milliseconds from sending the request to the answer or the failure.

attempted_at.description: When the request was sent. Its NR-Webhook-Timestamp is this time in Unix seconds.

WebhookDeliveryAttemptStatus.description: delivered when the endpoint answered 2xx; failed otherwise, with failure naming why.

WebhookDeliveryList.description: The 200 answer of GET /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/deliveries: one page of the endpoint's delivery attempts, newest first. Each item is one POST to the endpoint. Attempts are kept for 30 days, or the workspace's retention_days when that is shorter, and are deleted with the assessment they carried. next_cursor is present only when another page exists.

endpoint_id.description: Opaque id of the endpoint registration.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, MAC'd by the server and bound to the workspace and endpoint it was issued for. Pass it back unchanged as cursor; a tampered, foreign or expired cursor answers 400 invalid_cursor.

WebhookEndpoint.description: One of the workspace's registered webhook endpoints. Signing secrets are not part of it: a secret is shown once, when it is issued (POST /v1/webhooks and POST /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/rotate).

endpoint_id.description: Opaque id of the endpoint registration.

state.description: unverified until the endpoint echoes an endpoint.verification challenge (send one with POST /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/test); verified receives assessment.updated events; disabled after 72 hours of continuous delivery failure, and verified again by the same challenge.

response_mode.description: The view assessment.updated events carry: the assessment as GET /v1/assessments/{assessment_id} returns it in this response mode.

verified_at.description: When the endpoint last echoed a challenge. Absent until it first does.

failing_since.description: The first failed delivery attempt of the endpoint's current failure streak. Absent while its latest attempt succeeded, before any attempt failed, and after it is verified again.

last_failure_at.description: The latest failed delivery attempt of the current failure streak; present exactly when failing_since is. A failure more than 2 hours after it starts a new streak.

disabled_at.description: When the endpoint was disabled after failing continuously for 72 hours, as in the webhook_endpoint.disabled event. Present while state is disabled; absent before and after it is verified again.

signing_keys.description: The keys a receiver may see in NR-Webhook-Key-Id, oldest first. The last one signs every new delivery; an older one keeps verifying until its expires_at.

WebhookEndpointCreated.description: The 201 answer of POST /v1/webhooks: the new endpoint, unverified, and its first signing secret, shown once. Store the secret where the receiver reads it, then send endpoint.verification with POST /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/test.

WebhookEndpointDisabled.description: One of the environment's endpoints stopped receiving events: every delivery attempt to it failed from failing_since until disabled_at, 72 hours or more. Its queued deliveries are dropped. Fix the receiver and verify it again with POST /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/test (type endpoint.verification) to resume delivery.

disabled_at.description: When the endpoint was disabled; equal to the event's created_at.

id.description: The event id, equal to the NR-Webhook-Id header and across redeliveries and every endpoint the event fans out to.

created_at.description: When the event was created. Equal across redeliveries; the signing timestamp header is per delivery.

test.description: Present, and true, only on an event sent by POST /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/test: its data is a fixed example assessment, not one of the workspace's, so a receiver acknowledges it and applies nothing. Real events have no test member.

WebhookEndpointList.description: GET /v1/webhooks answer: every endpoint of the calling workspace, in every state, ordered by endpoint_id. A workspace holds at most 5, so there is no page.

WebhookEndpointRequest.description: POST /v1/webhooks body. The workspace is the API key that signs the request, so it is not a body member. The URL must be https on port 443 or 8443 with a DNS name, not an IP literal, and every address the name resolves to must be public.

url.description: Where deliveries are sent: an https URL on port 443 or 8443, with a DNS host and no userinfo or fragment, at most 2048 characters.

response_mode.description: The view assessment.updated events carry: standard (the default) or detailed, which needs an API key with the detailed scope as well.

WebhookEndpointState.description: unverified until the endpoint echoes an endpoint.verification challenge (send one with POST /v1/webhooks/{endpoint_id}/test); verified receives assessment.updated events; disabled after 72 hours of continuous delivery failure, and verified again by the same challenge.

Deliveries are at least once and unordered: deduplicate on id, and keep an assessment only when its detail.assessment_version is newer than the one you hold. GET /v1/assessments/{assessment_id} stays authoritative.

previous_key_id.description: The key that signed until this rotation.

previous_key_expires_at.description: When the previous key stops verifying: 7 days after the rotation.

AccountId.name: account_id

schema.description: Your own opaque identifier for the account being checked, scoped to your workspace. Use an id you mint, with no direct identifier (email, phone, name or national id) in it. '|' is accepted so an Auth0 user id such as 'auth0|64abc' passes unchanged; '@', '+', '$' and whitespace are refused by the pattern, as is an exact-shape JWT; a hex digest such as a SHA-256 is allowed, because hashing an internal id is a common pseudonymous scheme. A value such as '07700900123' or 'jane.doe.gmail.com' cannot be told apart from an opaque id. It travels in bodies, and in a URL only as the path segment of GET /v1/accounts/{account_id} and its /assessments. An assessment requested by a provider hook at pre_registration, which has no account yet, carries the server-issued account_id pre: followed by its assessment_id.
